questionText:
Read the following excerpt carefully and answer the question that follows:

"A contemporary article published in the Calcutta Review in 1856 analyzed the causes of the bloody Santhal insurrection (Hool): 'The Santhals were invited by the government from the 1830s to settle in the Damin-i-Koh, clear the dense sal forests and bring the land under the plough. By their untiring industry, barren hills were turned into fertile rice fields. But soon followed the unprincipled moneylenders and traders from the plains, whom the Santhals termed Dikus. The dikus charged exorbitant interest ranging from 50 to 500 percent, manipulated weights and measures, and seized Santhal lands through the collusion of corrupt police darogas. When all peaceful petitions to British magistrates failed, the brothers Sidhu and Kanhu declared that the gods had commanded them to liberate their ancestral country and establish an independent Santhal Raj.'"

What major administrative concession was granted by the British government after the Santhal rebellion was crushed?
